title: Work management (tasks, boards, workflows)
summary: Task and workflow tracking inside the legal app: work items linked to matters, shown as boards, lists and matter checklists, driven by configurable workflows, practice-area templates and automation rules, with team availability feeding workload. Its Clio counterparts are Manage tasks, task lists and Automated Workflows (and enterprise Clio Operate); Clio Work is an AI research and drafting workspace and maps to our documents and platform areas, not here. The agent is a first-class assignee that picks up items, shows its steps live, posts results and parks them in Needs approval; nothing it does reaches Done without a named human approval. Optional two-way sync with an external tracker through a generic connector.

screens.reg: RPC 6.1 supervision of delegated work (verify exact Ontario rule numbers): agent and non-lawyer outputs on legal work stay in Needs approval until a lawyer approves. Ethical walls (conflict screens) must hide items, not just disable them.

screens.agent: When assigned: reads matter context, does the work, streams a run log, posts output with cited sources, proposes a time entry, moves the item to Needs approval. On any item: summarizes long comment threads and suggests next step. Shows its step plan before running and a live step trace while running; can be stopped or redirected at any step.
screens.gate: Approver approves the agent's (or delegate's) output version; approval of outward-facing outputs (letters, filings, client emails) also triggers that module's own send/file gate.
edge: Output edited by approver before approving: store both versions, approval refers to edited version
Approver is the assignee (self-approval): blocked for agent items and for items whose template requires a second person
Matter reassigned to a new lawyer: open approvals re-route to the new responsible lawyer with a notice
Agent run exceeds budget/time: stops, posts partial output marked incomplete
Synced external item changed remotely while editing: field-level conflict banner
Client-visible item: internal comments never shown to the client; separate 'reply to client' composer
Recurring item completed late: next occurrence dates from the schedule, not from completion, unless set otherwise.
Private item assigned to the agent: agent output inherits privacy.
Category disabled: existing items keep it; it cannot be chosen again.
Assignee deactivated: open items move to the matter's responsible lawyer for reassignment.
Run stopped mid-step: no partial external action is taken; anything already drafted stays a draft.
Redirect changes a step into a regulated action: that step gets the 'needs approval' marker and waits at G-W1.
screens.reg: Supervision of delegated work (RPC ch. 6, verify). Privilege: comments are part of the matter file; client-visible flag must never leak internal notes. Records retention follows the matter.

actions.note: Lists affected items and deadlines and suggests the delegate per item; a human accepts.

actions.name: Warn on coverage gap
actions.note: Flags deadlines and approval-required items due while the owner and delegate are both away.

screens.agent: Builds the coverage-gap list, proposes delegates from team and workload, and warns deadline owners and responsible lawyers before an absence starts.
screens.gate: Supervising lawyer (or owner) approves an absence before it changes capacity, targets or coverage.
edge: Absence overlaps a critical deadline with no delegate: blocked from approval until a delegate is named or the lawyer accepts the risk with a reason.
Delegate lacks access to a walled matter: that matter's items fall back to its responsible lawyer.
Absence approved after items were reassigned manually: manual choices are kept.
Person deactivated: future absences are cancelled; offboarding is handled in the access area.
Admin sees absences and delegates only; the coverage-gaps list (item titles, matters, deadlines) is hidden from admin.
screens.reg: Coverage of a lawyer's practice during absence and supervision of delegated work (LSO) (verify).

open_questions: Should clients see and raise requests in the portal from day one, or staff-only in v1?
Is batch approval acceptable for routine internal items (summaries), or must every agent output be approved one by one?
Capacity unit for workload: hours (needs estimates) or item counts?
Is two-way external tracker sync in v1, or one-way export only? Which firms actually use Jira?
Do sub-tasks get their own approvals, or does the parent approval cover them?
Should time logged by the agent create proposed (unbilled) time entries by default, and at what rate?
SLA calendars: Ontario statutory holidays only, or firm-defined closures too?
Should automation rules be allowed to trigger the agent directly (e.g. 'draft reporting letter on stage Closed'), or only create items the agent then picks up? Current spec: only via items.
Is a firm-wide cap on automation rules needed for small firms, or just loop detection?
Allocation rules (queue per practice area, auto-assign by capacity and competency, human confirms for client work): worth adding to workload? (r09-people)
Should 'Ask a colleague to verify' also allow an opt-in external reviewer outside the firm? (r14-rivals)
Should imported Clio priorities High/Normal/Low map one-to-one to our default priorities? (r02-tasks-calendar)
Should work-reports show per-person upcoming/overdue/completed counts, with money productivity kept in time/utilization? (r09-people)
Canadian research content: CanLII link-out or a licence? Owned by platform/readiness research; listed here because research flagged it against work. (r14-rivals)
